0.0.n: An opening acknowledgment that gets the introduction started.

0.2.n: Sets the time for the tasting being described.

0.3.n: は makes today the topic, while ね adds a friendly conversational touch.

0.5.n: The name of a Japanese convenience store chain.

0.6.n: Links Lawson to its new products.

0.7.n: A compound combining 新, new, with 商品, products.

0.8.n: Usually groups people, but here playfully treats the products as a group.

0.9.n: Marks the new products as what the speaker ate.

0.10.n: Combines with 種類 to count different kinds.

0.11.n: Counts varieties rather than individual items.

0.12.n: 食べて plus みました expresses trying something, with a polite past ending.

1.0.n: Combines with も to include every choice.

1.1.n: After どれ, も makes the expression refer to all the items.

1.2.n: Part of どれもこれも, an emphatic expression including every single item.

1.3.n: Repeating も in どれもこれも emphasizes that there are no exceptions.

1.4.n: 甘い changes to 甘くて to connect it to another description.

1.5.n: A plain adjective describing how the products taste.

1.7.n: This subtitle fragment belongs to 美味しすぎて; 美味 is not a separate word here.

1.8.n: This fragment crosses the boundary between 美味し and すぎて in 美味しすぎて.

1.9.n: Starts midword in 美味しすぎて, then adds びっくり and an overwhelmed どうしよう, asking what to do.

2.0.n: Points back to the delighted reaction and introduces the summary という感じ.

2.1.n: In という感じ, it loosely sums up the situation or mood.

2.2.n: Connects that mood or situation to what happened next.

2.3.n: Adds a friendly pause while keeping the listener involved.

2.5.n: Used playfully before エネルギー to describe energy from happiness.

2.6.n: A borrowed word used figuratively for the good feeling gained from eating.

2.7.n: Marks the happy energy as what was absorbed.

2.8.n: Adds a conversational pause after the object without changing its role.

2.10.n: Describes the generous amount of energy absorbed.

2.11.n: Pairs with できました to say the speaker was able to absorb something.

2.12.n: The polite past form of できる expresses successful completion here.

3.0.n: A casual transition to the next part of the video.

3.1.n: Suggests making the most of the opportunity after trying all seven kinds.

3.2.n: A conversational shortening of なので that gives a reason, not the question word meaning why.

3.3.n: Softens the explanation and keeps the tone friendly.

3.5.n: Combines with 種類 to specify the number of varieties tasted.

3.6.n: Counts the different product varieties the speaker ate.

3.7.n: The plain past form of 食べる describes the seven kinds before 中.

3.8.n: Refers to the group of seven varieties already eaten.

3.9.n: Marks the group from which the top three are selected.

3.10.n: A borrowed word that combines with 3 to name the highest-ranked choices.

3.11.n: Specifies how many favorites will be announced.

3.12.n: Marks the top three as what the speaker will announce.

3.13.n: 発表する becomes 発表したい to express the speaker's wish.

3.14.n: Marks the preceding wish as the content of 思います.

3.15.n: The polite form of 思う softens the wish into a statement of intention.

4.0.n: Signals readiness to move straight into the announcement rather than literally meaning already.

4.1.n: Adds a casual, friendly beat before describing the pace.

4.3.n: An expressive sound suggesting several actions performed in rapid succession.

4.4.n: Turns the preceding expressive sound into a description of how the announcements will happen.

4.5.n: Adds another conversational pause before the main action.

4.7.m: want to go ahead and announce
4.7.n: 発表して plus いきたい expresses wanting to proceed with the announcements.

4.8.n: Links the intended action to 思います as what the speaker is thinking.

4.9.n: The polite ending makes the intention sound softer than a direct declaration.

0.lit: All right, today, you know, I tried eating seven kinds of Lawson's new products.
0.tip: A verb's て-form plus みる means trying that action to see what it is like.

1.lit: Every one, this one too, sweet and delicious. So delicious I'm surprised; what should I do?
1.tip: 美味しすぎて means so delicious that; the subtitle splits this expression into fragments that are not separate words.

2.lit: With that sort of feeling, you know, I was able to absorb plenty of happiness energy.
2.tip: 吸収できました means was able to absorb, combining an action noun with できる.

3.lit: Well then, since I've gone to the trouble, I think I want to announce the top three from seven kinds eaten.
3.tip: たいと思います is a polite, softened way to state what you intend to do.

4.lit: Now, you know, rapidly, you know, I think I want to go ahead and announce them.
4.tip: An expressive sound followed by と can describe how an action is performed.
